adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category site setting is blank/never set (the default), because execute(...)[0] is nil and nil['id'] is dereferenced
Migration assumes embeddable_hosts setting is newline-delimited text but it's a serialized host_list (YAML array), so splitting yields garbage records inserted verbatim

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows prior code treated `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` as a newline-delimited string: the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` method repeatedly does `embeddable_hosts.split("\n")` and compares hosts. The migration similarly reads the `site_settings.value` (a DB string) and splits on newlines. There’s no evidence in this diff that `embeddable_hosts` was stored as a YAML-serialized array, so the claim that splitting would insert “garbage records” isn’t verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration insert uses raw string interpolation '#{h}', so any quote in the value causes a SQL syntax error

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any host line `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid (syntax error) and can also allow SQL injection in the context of the migration since the value is not quoted/escaped by the DB adapter. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses cmd_tuples (a PG::Result method) but ActiveRecord execute on MySQL returns a plain Array, crashing on MySQL

adjudication.rationale: The migration does call `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples`, which is specific to PostgreSQL’s `PG::Result`. However, this codebase (Discourse) runs on PostgreSQL only, and elsewhere in the same migration it already relies on PG-style results (e.g., `execute(...)[0]['id']`). Within the supported DB environment, `cmd_tuples` is valid and won’t crash. The reported “crashing on MySQL” is not a verifiable problem for this diff because MySQL isn’t a supported target here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id' may return zero rows, making [0]['value'] another nil dereference

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the fallback branch does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` without checking whether the query returned any rows. If the `site_settings` table does not contain a row for `uncategorized_category_id` (e.g., depending on how settings are persisted in that installation/version), `[0]` will be `nil` and `['value']` will raise, breaking the migration. The diff introduces this unchecked dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding controller update action never reads params or saves anything, so the PUT save path is a no-op and client-side mutations are silently lost

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` after `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). It does not read `params`, does not modify any model, and does not persist anything. A PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` is therefore a no-op. The client controller even defines `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, which would hit that PUT endpoint, but there is nothing server-side to apply/save even if it were invoked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js _ids branch maps missing sub-type lookups to false/undefined and assigns the array as-is; || [] fallback only triggers when every lookup fails, so partially side-loaded payloads produce arrays with false holes causing template crashes

adjudication.rationale: In store.js, the new `_ids` handling does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), the `|| []` fallback never removes missing lookups; any `_lookupSubType` misses become `undefined`/`null` elements in the array. The code also unconditionally `delete obj[k]`, so you lose the original ids even if some lookups fail. This can lead to partially-hydrated arrays containing holes, which can plausibly break consumers/templates expecting every entry to be an object (e.g. iterating and accessing properties).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb crashes on fresh installs because the embed_category inner-join query returns zero rows, making [0] nil and raising NoMethodError before the fallback is reached

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the first lookup does `execute(... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category' )[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns no rows (likely on fresh installs where there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category`), `[...] [0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The fallback `if category_id == 0` is never reached because the exception occurs before `category_id` can be computed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb interpolates host values raw into the INSERT SQL without escaping, so hosts containing apostrophes produce invalid SQL and abort the migration midway

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops over `records.each do |h|` (where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts`) and executes:

```rb
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

`h` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL string with no escaping/quoting helper. If `h` contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid and the migration will error/abort. More generally, this is unsafe raw SQL interpolation (potential SQL injection) even if the expected host format normally wouldn’t include quotes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT but changes nothing and returns success, making it a silent no-op with missing persistence logic (or dead code)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or performs any mutation/persistence. Yet routes explicitly add `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember controller has an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this PUT endpoint. As written, that PUT will always “succeed” while saving nothing, i.e., a silent no-op/dead persistence endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost model lacks a uniqueness validation and unique index, allowing duplicate hosts with different categories where record_for_host returns an arbitrary first match

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost` only validates host format and trims scheme/path, but does not enforce uniqueness of `host` (no `validates_uniqueness_of` and the migration creates no unique index). Lookup paths like `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(host)` use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will return an arbitrary matching row if duplicates exist. This matters because `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` to pick the category for embedded topics, so duplicates with different `category_id` make behavior nondeterministic and can mis-route posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController update and destroy don't check host.present?, so nil records from stale ids raise unhandled 500s instead of 404/422
Host validation permits ports but record_for_host compares against uri.host (port stripped), so hosts saved with ports never match and the feature silently fails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` validation allows an optional port (`...(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and the `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does **not** strip `:port`, so a record can be saved as e.g. `example.com:3000`. However `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the input with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means `example.com:3000` in the DB will never match `uri.host == "example.com"`, causing `host_allowed?` to return false and embedding to fail for port-specified hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs only assert class ancestry with zero functional verification of CRUD endpoints, error rendering, fallbacks, or nil-id 404 paths; no JS tests for the embeddable-host component either

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) that only assert the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController` and do not exercise any actions (create/update/destroy/show), error cases, or 404/nil handling. The diff also adds a substantial Ember component/controller/route for embedding/embeddable-hosts, but introduces no corresponding JS/acceptance/component tests in this change. This is a verifiable gap in functional test coverage for newly added behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic#expandable_first_post? dropped the embeddable_hosts.present? guard, changing behavior for hostless sites that still have topic_embeds with embed_truncate enabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but `embeddable_hosts` as a site setting is also removed entirely (site_settings.yml entry deleted and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` removed). Embedding authorization is now based on the `EmbeddableHost` model, and `expandable_first_post?` is only checking whether truncation is enabled and the topic actually has an embed (`has_topic_embed?`). There’s no clear defect shown: for existing embedded topics, allowing expand/collapse when `embed_truncate` is on is reasonable even if there are currently zero allowed hosts. The finding assumes this behavior is wrong, but the diff doesn’t establish that invariant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration deletes site settings via raw SQL without flushing SiteSetting's in-process cache, leaving long-running processes with stale phantom values

adjudication.rationale: The migration does delete `site_settings` rows via raw SQL (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`), but the diff also removes runtime usage of those settings (`SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` is deleted and callers now use `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`; `embed_category` setting is removed from `site_settings.yml` and `TopicEmbed` now derives category from `EmbeddableHost`). Since the application code in this diff no longer relies on the deleted settings, an in-process `SiteSetting` cache being stale for those keys would not cause a verifiable defect attributable to this change. The finding is therefore speculative/not a concrete problem shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents swapped: category fabricators moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host fabricator into category_fabricator.rb, breaking convention-based tooling and future edits
admin/embedding_controller.rb update action is a no-op endpoint that fetches and re-renders the embedding without applying any params — dead code

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads or applies any `params`, and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (not persisted). The client controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which will hit this PUT endpoint but cannot actually save anything. So the diff introduces an update endpoint/action that is effectively a no-op and makes the “saveChanges” path non-functional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded in store.js.es6 is core shared infrastructure modified globally to hydrate any *_ids key, expanding scope beyond the feature's requirement

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify shared store infrastructure: `_hydrateEmbedded` changes its regex from `/(.+)_id$/` to `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` and adds special handling that will delete any `*_ids` key and replace it with `pluralize(subType)` containing hydrated records. However, the proposed finding frames this as a definite problem (“expanding scope beyond the feature's requirement”), which is not verifiable from the diff alone: there’s no demonstrated incorrect behavior or known conflicting `*_ids` payload usage shown here. It’s a potentially risky broad change, but the claim of it being a real defect is speculative without evidence of breakage in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration dereferences [0] on the embed_category query result unconditionally, crashing with NoMethodError when no category matches (empty/renamed settings)
Migration string-interpolates raw embeddable_hosts site-setting values into SQL INSERT, breaking on quote characters instead of using parameterized inserts
update action on missing id calls host.destroy/nil.host on nil, causing 500 instead of 404 when a host was already deleted

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id is missing/invalid (or the host was already deleted), this returns `nil`. The code then calls methods on it (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`), which will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host, allowing duplicate host rows; record_for_host .first makes category selection nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbeddableHost model/migration does not enforce uniqueness of `host` at either the model level (no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`) or DB level (migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with no unique index on `host`). Lookups use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(...).where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so if duplicate rows exist for the same host (case-insensitively), `.first` will pick an arbitrary row depending on DB ordering, making the associated category used in `TopicEmbed.import` (`category: eh.try(:category_id)`) potentially nondeterministic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action crashes with NoMethodError when embeddable_host param is missing, returning 500 instead of 400
EmbeddingController#update never applies params, so the Save Changes button silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does just re-render the serialized embedding and does not apply any params. However, the new `embedding.hbs` template does not include any “Save Changes” button or call the `saveChanges` action at all; the only UI actions shown are per-host save/delete (handled via `EmbeddableHost` records) and “Add Host”. The JS `saveChanges()` action exists but is unused in this diff, so the claim that a Save Changes button “silently does nothing” is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration lacks unique index on host, index on category_id, and FK; record_for_host lower(host) lookup is a full table scan on the hot embed path, and create path never downcases so case-variant duplicates are allowed

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts(host, category_id, ...)` without any indexes, uniqueness constraint, or foreign key. Yet runtime lookups on the embed path call `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`; with no index this will be a full table scan, and even with a normal index the `lower(host)` expression would not use it unless a functional index exists. Also, neither `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` nor `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` downcases the host; since the column is not unique/case-insensitive, case-variant duplicates can be created, and `first` would pick an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. `category_id` likewise has no index/foreign key despite being a required association.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hostname regex validation rejects valid hosts like localhost, TLDs > 5 chars, and punycode, breaking previously accepted embed hosts

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbeddableHost model adds `validates_format_of :host` with a regex requiring a dotted domain and a TLD of 2–5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), which will reject hosts like `localhost` (no dot) and modern/IDN/punycode TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.museum`, many `xn--...` forms). Previously, the allow-check logic in `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` compared parsed `URI(host).host` against the configured list and did not impose this 2–5 letter TLD restriction, so this diff introduces a real behavioral restriction that can break previously acceptable embed hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation uses sub! on possibly non-String host, crashing on nil, and normalization of case never happens so stored-case vs lookup-case mismatch is papered over by lower()
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `before_validation` calls `sub!` on `host` which may be `nil`, causing a crash/NoMethodError. This is the same core issue as the golden comment (nil `self.host` leading to `sub!` failure), though it adds an extra note about case normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb category from embed host is nil when host not in table, so topics silently post to uncategorized instead of falling back to embed_category setting
host.save success path: Discourse.Category.findById throws if categoryId is null, and returns undefined for uncategorized leaving badge rendering broken

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')`, but `categoryId` starts as `null` and is only set in `edit()` from `host.category.id`. For a new host (or if the user leaves the chooser blank), `categoryId` can remain null. The server explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, but on success the client does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` which uses the possibly-null pre-save value rather than the persisted `category_id`. That leaves `host.category` unset/undefined even though the record is saved with a category, so `{{category-badge host.category}}` can render incorrectly (blank). The claim that `findById` "throws" on null is not proven by this diff, but the mismatch/defaulting bug is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: REST adapter type.replace('_','-') rewrites all type names; embeddable-host createRecord may 404 against /admin/embeddable_hosts due to unverified pluralization, plus parallel-path asymmetry of two adapters/endpoints
EmbeddingSerializer embed: :ids hydrated subtypes are plain store objects without .save, so host.save(props) may throw on save
Migration crashes on fresh installs when embed_category setting row is absent (execute result nil['id'])

adjudication.rationale:
In migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it does:

```rb
category_id = execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If the query returns zero rows (e.g., on a fresh install where the `embed_category` setting row is absent—especially since `embed_category` is removed from `config/site_settings.yml` in this diff), `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil`, and `nil['id']` will raise an exception before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. That makes the migration crash in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection/quote-breaking in migration INSERT via unescaped interpolation of setting value and category_id

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from `site_settings` (`embeddable_hosts` value split by newlines). If any stored host line contains a single quote (or crafted SQL), it will break quoting and could alter the SQL executed. This is a verifiable quote-breaking / injection risk introduced by the diff; `category_id` is coerced to integer so the main risk is the unescaped `h`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stacked didInsertElement and editing observers cause _focusOnInput to run when editing turns off, plus categoryId mirror state can drift from host.category.id
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites where embed_category site setting was never set, because execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] assumes the row exists
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the migration assumes execute(...)[0]['id'] exists for the embed_category setting, and will crash (NoMethodError) when the query returns no rows because the site setting was never set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration irreversibly deletes site settings rows (embeddable_hosts, embed_category) with no down path, permanently losing admin-configured hosts and category if rollback or mis-import occurs

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses `def change` and runs raw SQL `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Raw `execute` statements are not automatically reversible by Rails, and there is no explicit `down` method to restore the deleted rows. This makes the migration effectively irreversible and permanently removes those site settings values if rollback is attempted or if the import into `embeddable_hosts` is wrong/incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped string interpolation of raw setting values into INSERT SQL; a host value containing a quote breaks the INSERT or corrupts the row; should use sanitized/quoted values
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core problem: building an SQL statement via unescaped string interpolation (e.g., inserting host/setting values directly into an INSERT), which can be broken by quotes and is susceptible to SQL injection. Both recommend using quoting/sanitization or parameter binding instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a silent no-op that persists nothing while the UI exposes a save action, so admins click save, get success, and nothing changes

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed does not persist anything (it just re-renders the serialized `@embedding` OpenStruct). However, the claim that “the UI exposes a save action” is not verifiable from this diff: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains only the hosts table and an “Add Host” button, and never calls the controller’s `saveChanges` action. Host persistence is handled via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save` / `destroyRecord`) instead. So while the update endpoint is effectively a no-op, the specific user-facing defect described (admins click save, get success, nothing changes) is not demonstrated by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update (and destroy) uses where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, causing NoMethodError/500 on stale or unknown ids instead of 404
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate highlights that update/destroy fetch the record via `where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil, leading to a NoMethodError/500 for missing IDs instead of handling (e.g., 404). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricators were moved into the wrong file: the contents of category_fabricator.rb (including :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) now live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa, a misleading naming inversion
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are in the wrong files (effectively swapped), causing a naming inversion and implying potential misuse/errors. This matches the golden issue of swapped file contents and loss/misplacement of the original category fabricators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? guard SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? was removed, widening expand behavior to any topic with a topic_embed when embed_truncate is on, silently changing rendering for pre-existing topics

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, changing the condition from `embeddable_hosts.present? && embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. However, `embeddable_hosts` site setting is also removed entirely (migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table), so the old guard no longer represents the new configuration mechanism. The method still only applies to topics that already have a `topic_embed` (`has_topic_embed?`), so it does not widen behavior to non-embedded topics. Whether existing embedded topics should lose “expandable” behavior when the allowed-host list becomes empty is product/behavioral, not a clear defect introduced by this diff, and the finding’s claim of a “real problem” isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic imports now take category from EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) instead of global embed_category; unmatched feed URLs land topics in uncategorized, silently changing destination category for existing feed-polling installs

SQL string interpolation of unsanitized admin-entered embeddable_hosts setting value in migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 29, allowing broken migrations or SQL injection; should use sanitize_sql/quote or EmbeddableHost.create!

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the existing site_settings value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, then runs raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is inserted directly inside single quotes with no quoting/escaping, any host value containing `'` (or crafted SQL) can break the migration or alter the executed SQL. Even if the value is typically admin-entered, it is still unsanitized data coming from the DB and should be quoted (e.g., `connection.quote(h)`) or inserted via AR (`EmbeddableHost.create!`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs (embedding_controller_spec.rb, embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb) only assert class inheritance, verifying nothing about behavior; EmbeddingController#update never mutates @embedding yet the client calls saveChanges, and no test catches this
No test for EmbeddableHost validation failure path (invalid host strings) or the controller's host.save failure branch; the host format regex has no coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with a `validates_format_of :host` regex and an admin controller `save_host` method with an explicit failure branch (`else render_json_error(host)`). The added model spec (`spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`) only tests trimming behavior and `host_allowed?` for valid hosts, and does not include any example asserting invalid host strings are rejected (i.e., exercising the regex failure). The added controller specs only check subclassing and do not test `create/update` with invalid params to hit the `host.save` failure branch. So the stated lack of coverage is accurate and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host untested for malformed/non-URI input and its false return; TopicEmbed.import path where eh is nil (topic posts to nil category) is untested
expandable_first_post? dropped the host check but the spec still fabricates an embeddable host in a before block, documenting the wrong invariant (mirror-test)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but the provided diff hunk for `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` is truncated right as the `describe "expandable_first_post?"` section begins. Within the visible changes, there is no fabricated `embeddable_host` in a `before` block (or any host-related setup) that can be verified. Also, even if such setup existed, it would be a test smell/misleading invariant rather than a product bug introduced by the code change. So the proposed finding is not verifiably supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed controller's referer-check reject branch with a populated EmbeddableHost table and a foreign referer is untested

Migration data transfer of embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings into rows has zero test coverage; the name-based category join silently falls to uncategorized when a category was renamed, untested

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` derives `category_id` via a SQL join `s.value = c.name` for `s.name = 'embed_category'`. If the stored site setting value doesn’t exactly match the current category name (e.g., the category was renamed), the query yields no row, `to_i` becomes `0`, and the migration silently falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`. That can incorrectly migrate existing embedding configuration. There are no specs covering this migration behavior (only controller/model specs were added), so this edge case is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New admin UI component/controller/adapter (embeddable-host.js.es6) with ~100 lines of save/cancel/edit/cantSave/pathFor logic has zero JS tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add new Ember admin adapter/component/controller/route/template files, and it does not include any corresponding JavaScript/Ember test files (only Ruby specs were added). However, “has zero JS tests” is a process/coverage comment rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself, and the diff doesn’t show a project requirement being violated (e.g., failing/removed JS tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural path only tested with well-formed ids; dangling plural ids (missing sidecar object) yield undefined entries in the hydrated array, untested, and the || [] fallback is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural hydration branch in `store.js.es6`, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array, even if every `_lookupSubType` call returns `undefined`/`null` (e.g., when an id has no matching sidecar object in `root`). That means the code can silently replace `*_ids` with an array containing `undefined` entries (`obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated`), and it also always deletes the original ids (`delete obj[k]`), losing information in that scenario. Additionally, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead/unreachable because `map` never returns a falsy value; it returns an Array object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration irreversibly deletes site_settings rows ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') with no backup or down-migration, making data unrecoverable on rollback

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses a `change` method with raw `execute` statements to copy values out of `site_settings` and then runs `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no explicit `down` migration to restore those rows, and Rails cannot automatically reverse arbitrary `execute` SQL (especially destructive deletes). Even if the table creation were reverted, the deleted `site_settings` data would not be восстановable on rollback, making the migration effectively irreversible and data-lossy when rolling back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when 'embed_category' setting is unset because [0]['id'] dereferences nil

adjudication.rationale:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If the `embed_category` site setting is unset/blank or doesn’t match any category name, the SQL returns zero rows, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. The later `if category_id == 0` fallback can’t run because the exception happens first. This is a real crash risk introduced by the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback lookup queries nonexistent 'uncategorized_category_id' site_settings row, so [0]['value'] raises NoMethodError and the fallback path is broken

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the fallback query is `SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'` and then `[0]['value']`. The diff does not show that this site setting row is removed or doesn't exist; in fact, the codebase continues to rely on `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` elsewhere, which strongly implies the setting exists in normal installs. Therefore the claim that the fallback lookup targets a nonexistent row is not verifiable from the diff and is likely a misreading/speculation. (There is a separate potential issue: other `execute(...)[0]` calls can raise if the result set is empty, but that is not what the finding asserts.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill INSERT interpolates raw host values unescaped, so hosts with single quotes break the SQL and risk a partially-applied migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the backfill loop builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` and is not escaped/quoted safely. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail mid-way, leaving a partially-applied migration (table created, some rows inserted, settings not deleted). This is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table uses force: true, silently dropping any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and its data

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will DROP the table if it already exists and recreate it, which would remove any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` data. So the finding accurately describes behavior introduced by the diff (even if the table is expected to be new).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_hosts.category_id has no foreign key or dependent cleanup, leaving orphaned references when a category is deleted

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with a non-null `category_id` column but does not add a foreign key constraint to `categories` (no `add_foreign_key`), and the `EmbeddableHost` model only has `belongs_to :category` with no dependent behavior. Nothing in this diff updates category deletion logic to clean up or nullify `embeddable_hosts.category_id`. Therefore, deleting a category can leave existing `embeddable_hosts` rows pointing at a non-existent category (an orphaned reference), which is exactly what the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill matches category by name instead of id, which can miss or silently assign the wrong category

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The backfill in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb determines category_id via `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`, i.e. it matches the site setting value against `categories.name` rather than an id. If `embed_category` stored an id (common for category settings) or if category names are not unique / have changed, the query returns no row (category_id becomes 0 and it silently falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`) or could pick an unintended category. This is a concrete correctness risk introduced by the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No deploy-window safety for removed embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings: rolling deploys crash on removed constants and TopicEmbed.import falls back to nil/default category instead of the old per-site default
